title: After a run ends, the Started line stays and Go does not return until reload (state.go stays running)
description:
After a run ends, the task page keeps its "Started." line and does not bring the Go button back until the page is reloaded. It happens on unfinished tasks and on Home, not only on finished ones.

## Why it matters

A user who watches a run finish sees a stale "Started." state and no way to start the next run until they reload. Every run on every task goes through this, so it recurs. It costs a reload, not a run, so it is a papercut.

## What is happening

`state.go` stays `running` after the run poll stops (`runPoll`, `public/prompt-section.js`, around lines 2312-2333). `runPoll` calls `paintState()` and `paintGo()` while `state.go` is started or running, but nothing moves `state.go` out of `running` when the run ends. LIN-4048 (PR #2284, merged as c70b004c) made the task-page run slot repaint on that poll, which fixed the stale Stop / runs-on. It did not touch `state.go`, on purpose, because fixing it brings Go back on unfinished tasks, which is a separate decision.

## Acceptance

* On the task page, when a held run ends, the Started line goes and Go returns (when the server's offer allows it) without a reload.
* A finished task still shows no Go: the server's `none` from `runOfferOf` (`lib/task-state.js`) stays the only decider.
* A test fails before the change and passes after. `tests/e2e/lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js` is the pattern for ending a held run in a real browser.

## Anchors

* `public/prompt-section.js`: `runPoll`, `paintGo`, `paintState`, `state.go`
* `lib/task-state.js`: `runOfferOf`
* Related: LIN-3341 (Go is one press), LIN-4048 (found it, excluded it)

## Unvalidated idea

When the poll sees the run is no longer held, reset `state.go` to idle and repaint Go from the server's offer. Check Home and Swipe, which share `renderGo`.

Priority reasoning: Medium. Every run hits it, but a reload clears it and no run is spent.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

Both Surveys (on this ticket, 10:17, at `29f14bf6e`) agree on where this binds, and that a plain "reset `state.go` when the poll stops" would be wrong. The person's scope call, in pieces, in order:

1. **The e2e first, red.** From `tests/e2e/lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js`'s `seedHeldRun` plus the feedback that ends it, on an **unfinished** task: on the task page **and on Home**, the rungs come back and `opened-task-started` goes within about 25 s. Assert on `opened-task-go` and the rung testids.
2. **One rule for "the run has ended", from the server's fields:** a *complete* `/state` reply (`!data.incomplete`) with nothing in progress (`!sessions.busy`, i.e. stay while the offer's kind is `busy`), shared by `runPoll` and the mount read. That also covers:
   * an incomplete reply keeps polling, as `task-page.js`'s `createPoller` does, rather than ending the run;
   * the started-but-not-yet-visible race (a first read before the queued item reaches the gather) doesn't bring Go back for a queued run.

   Add a vm unit for "incomplete → still running", which the e2e can't easily produce.
3. **One** `endRun()`**:** `state.go` back to ready, clear `state.run.item` (Home's run box stays active on it otherwise) and the started notice, then `paintRun()` and `paintGo()`. All three presses (Go, Next step, run-step) share `runPoll`, so one reset covers them. Swipe repaints through `paintGo`.
4. **Flip the test that pins today's choice** (`tests/unit/prompt-section-go.test.js:283`, "the run ended; keep the last sentence"); don't add a second one beside it. Update the Go-states comment (about lines 237–247) to say how Go leaves "started/running".

* A finished task still shows no Go: `renderGo` checks `takesNoRun` first, so `runOfferOf`'s `none` stays the only decider. Keep a test showing it.

**Not in this ticket:** Go's displayed state following `/state` entirely, with `state.go` kept only for the press itself; moving the run control out of `prompt-section.js`; sharing one "ended" rule with `cadenceStatus`.

## At merge (who else must learn about it)

* Go's "in progress" is no longer answered by `goInProgress` on its own. Say what is left of the three answers (`goInProgress`, `stageBusy`, the offer's `busy`).
* `llms.txt`, if it describes the started line or Go's states.
* No new file without an obvious home.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2289](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2289>) (merged as b5cc4c62): `runEnded` (one end rule: a complete `/state` reply that is neither live/waiting nor `sessions.busy`) and `endRun` (Go back to ready, `run.item` cleared, run block and Go repainted) in `public/prompt-section.js`; `runPoll` follows the rule and drops a stale read; the pinned unit test was flipped; the Go-states comment and `public/llms.txt:295` were updated; e2e witnesses for the task page and Home. Deviations: none in design; close-out added the Home `opened-task-queued` assertion (f5a4f157) that review asked for. The full plan, cause analysis and witness list are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail; the unmet-by-design follow-up (Go following `/state` entirely) is LIN-4256.

### Session fit and review

fits one session (one file, its tests, one e2e spec, two doc lines).
plan-review due: no (it loosens no validation or contract).

comments.body:
## Survey global: LIN-4247 @ 29f14bf6e

(LinearViewer `origin/main`)

**Where it lands.** In `public/prompt-section.js` (2,885 lines), in Go's lifecycle: `runPoll`, `setGoRunning`, `goInProgress`, `paintGo` and the mount read. The file is improving on *who decides*. LIN-4016, 4068, 4071 and 4104 moved the run decision to the server (`sessions.action` / `runOfferOf`), and `renderGo` checks `takesNoRun` before its other branches. Go's *lifecycle* didn't get the same treatment. It still uses its own client-side "in progress" test (`goInProgress`: `live || status==='waiting'`), alongside `stageBusy` (`sessions.busy`) and the offer's `busy` kind. That's three answers to one question. The file grows a ticket at a time.

**The current behaviour was chosen on purpose.** `runPoll` ends with `// else: the run ended; keep the last sentence and stop polling.`, and `tests/unit/prompt-section-go.test.js:283` pins it. The fix reverses that test, so change that test instead of adding a second one beside it.

**Done the obvious way** (in `runPoll`'s else branch, set `state.go = {status:'ready'}` and call `paintGo()`):
- Task page: the Go slot sits inside the run block, and `paintState`→`paintRun` already redraws `renderGo` from the fresh `sessions.action`. So `none` stays the only thing that decides a finished task.
- **Home has a second flag that sticks.** Its run box is active while `summary.running || state.run.item` (line 1618). `state.run.item` only clears when a read sees `sessions.running` (line 1089) or Stop succeeds. If a short run ends before the first 10s poll, Home keeps the active box, with "Started.", even after `state.go` resets. Clear `state.run.item` when the run ends as well, or Home stays broken.
- Three presses set `started`: Go, Next step (~1722) and run-step (~1776). All three share `runPoll`, so one reset covers them all. Swipe has no run block, so it repaints through `paintGo`.
- An `incomplete` `/state` read has no `live`, so the poll already stops *as if the run ended*. With a reset, Go could reappear in the middle of a run. Only reset on a complete read.
- Go's states are documented only in the comment at lines 237-247. Its "started/running" line should say how Go leaves that state.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry.** Decide "the run ended" from the server's fields (`!data.incomplete && !data.sessions.busy`), not `goInProgress`, and share one helper between the poll and the mount read. Reset `state.go` and `state.run.item` together in one `endRun()`. For the e2e, extend the LIN-4048 spec's `seedHeldRun` + feedback-ends-it pattern to an *unfinished* task, on the task page and on Home.

**Better still, but not this task's.** Have Go's displayed state follow `/state` entirely, and keep `state.go` only for the press itself (`starting`, a refusal notice). "Started." and the poll's own stop rule would then disappear. That reworks the run block on three surfaces, which is the natural time to move the run control out of `prompt-section.js`.

## Survey open-0: LIN-4247 @ 29f14bf6e

Read at `29f14bf6e` (LinearViewer `origin/main`).

**Why it's harder than "reset `state.go` when the poll ends"**

1. **`runPoll` ends the run on a reply that isn't an ending.** `goInProgress` is `live === true || status === 'waiting'`. An `incomplete` `/state` reply (`routes/task-page.js` ~229) carries neither field, so `runPoll` (`prompt-section.js` ~2342) stops polling there. It has no `headerHtml` either, so "Started." is never replaced. The page's own poller (`task-page.js` `createPoller`) keeps the last complete status and reads again soon. My guess is that this is where a lasting "Started." comes from (subtask trees, cold gathers). A complete read already blanks it on the task surface. A plain reset whenever `goInProgress` is false would bring Go back mid-run on an incomplete reply. "Ended" has to mean a **complete** reply with nothing in progress.

2. **Started-but-not-yet-visible race.** Go and the step presses set `started` straight after the 201. If the first read lands before the queued item reaches the gather, it reads not-live, and a reset would offer Go for a run that's already queued. `DUPLICATE_DISPATCH` stops a double run, but the UI flickers. Either require one in-progress read before trusting not-live, or decide from `sessions.action.kind` (stay while `busy`).

3. **Three surfaces, three repaint paths.** On the task page, Go sits in the run block (`paintRun`). On Home it's in the run box (only when `runBox && runControlOn()`). Swipe has no run control, so only `paintGo` reaches it. Repaint one slot and another surface stays stale. On Home and the task page, "Go" is now the three rungs, so tests should assert on `opened-task-go` and the rung testids.

4. **Leftovers.** `state.run.item` and the started notice ("Nothing is listening…") need clearing too, or they outlive the run.

The finished-task bullet is nearly free: `renderGo` checks `takesNoRun` first.

**What I'd do first**

Write the e2e from `lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js`: on an open task, press Run to PR (or mount with a held run), end it with the feedback post, and expect the rungs back and `opened-task-started` gone within about 25s (the poll is a fixed 10s). Then make `runPoll` keep polling on incomplete replies, as `createPoller` does. After that, add one reset helper (go → ready, clear `run.item` and the notice, `paintRun()` + `paintGo()`) that runs only on a complete, not-in-progress reply. Add a vm-sandbox unit for incomplete → still running, since the e2e can't easily produce an incomplete reply.

It's a symptom of something deeper: two pollers read the same `/state` with different rules for "ended". Sharing `cadenceStatus`-style rules is the real fix, but I'd keep that refactor out of this ticket.

## LIN-4247: implemented, PR open, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2289 (branch `feat/lin-4247-run-end-go-returns`, commit bff94e0b)

**Cause:** `runPoll` stopped on any reply that was not live, so nothing moved `state.go` out of running. Home's `state.run.item` also kept its box active.

**Change (`public/prompt-section.js`):**
- One end rule, `runEnded`: a complete `/state` reply that is neither live/waiting nor `sessions.busy`. An incomplete reply is never an end.
- One reset, `endRun`: Go back to ready, `run.item` cleared, then paint the run block and Go.
- Finished tasks unchanged: `renderGo` still draws the server's `none` offer.
- A poll read that lands after Go changed is dropped, so a stale read cannot end a newer run.

**Evidence:**
- Unit: the pinned "keep the last sentence" test is flipped, not duplicated. New witnesses for incomplete, complete-but-busy, finished task and stale read. Full unit suite: 23,294 pass, 0 fail.
- E2E: a task-page witness and a Home witness (Run to PR). Both fail on the unfixed code and pass with the change.
- CI on the PR: all checks pass (unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, secret scan, `CI success`).

**Known cost:** the poll now continues while `sessions.busy` is true (a subtree runs), where it used to stop at not-live. Same 10 s read; it ends with the page.

## Review — LIN-4247

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2289, reviewed at head `bff94e0b` (one commit on base `29f14bf6`).

CI: green on `bff94e0b` (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, CI success). I also re-ran `prompt-section-go.test.js` (30/30) and `lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js` (5/5) locally on that head.

### Scope against the plan
The diff matches the plan's places. It touches `public/prompt-section.js` (`runEnded`, `endRun`, `runPoll` and the Go-states comment), `public/llms.txt:295`, the LIN-4048 e2e spec and `prompt-section-go.test.js`. There is no new file. The mount read and the press-time read still use `goInProgress` alone, as decision 4 says. Every point in the plan's Direction has an implementing line:
- incomplete reply → poll continues;
- complete + `sessions.busy` → poll continues;
- ended reply → `endRun` before the header write (so it cannot set Go back to running);
- the stale-read guard (`state.go !== reading`).

**Staleness check.** `git log --since=2026-11-05T04:51Z` over `prompt-section.js`, `lib/task-state.js` and `routes/task-page.js` on main is empty, so the ticket still describes the code.

**Regression check.** LIN-4048 (`c70b004c`, `paintState` → `paintRun`) is intact: its Done-task e2e tests still pass. Nothing here re-applies a reverted change.

**Queued-race claim.** `/state`'s `sessions.busy` comes from the gather's `UNENDED_STATES = {running, queued, waiting}` (`lib/task-state.js:28,64`). A queued item therefore reads busy, so it is not treated as ended.

**Stale guard.** I checked every `state.go` writer. Each one that enters started/running calls `startPoll()`: `setGoRunning`, the step presses, Go's press, and Stop's `.then`. The others (`refuseStale`, `applyGoRefusal`) set ready. So dropping a stale read can never leave Go running with no poll.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| remove `if (runEnded(data)) { endRun(); return; }` | 2 unit tests red; both new e2e tests red (the pre-fix behaviour) |
| `runEnded` treats `incomplete` as an end | the "no sessions at all" unit test red |
| `runEnded` ignores `sessions.busy` | the complete-but-busy unit test red |
| remove the `state.go !== reading` guard | the stale-read unit test red |
| **remove `state.run.item = null` from `endRun`** | **every unit test and every e2e test stays green** |
| **remove `paintRun()` from `endRun`** | **every unit test and every e2e test stays green** |

The Home e2e was written as the witness for `run.item` (plan, witness 1). With `run.item` left set, Home's box stays active and shows **"Queued, waiting for a runner · Undo"** (`opened-task-queued`, `renderAfterRun`) for the finished item. The test asserts on `opened-task-started`, `opened-task-running` and `opened-task-go`, but not on that line. So it passes whether or not the fix is there.

I tried one line: `await expect(block.locator('[data-testid="opened-task-queued"]')).toHaveCount(0);`, placed after the `opened-task-running` assertion. It passes on `bff94e0b` and goes **red under both mutations above**. The fix is listed below.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "a client poller with its own rule for when a run has ended".
- `task-page.js`'s `createPoller` already continues on incomplete replies. Not affected.
- `cadenceStatus`, and making Go's display follow `/state` entirely, were explicitly put out of scope by the ticket's "Not in this ticket" list and the Survey. Both are **outside**. The plan says to file them if no ticket exists, and that is close-out's job.

No other writer ends `state.go`. Within this ticket the change is complete.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (plan's witness 1, Home `state.run.item`; plan Direction 2). Nothing currently proves that Home's queued/run box clears when a short run ends. **Before the merge**, add the assertion `await expect(block.locator('[data-testid="opened-task-queued"]')).toHaveCount(0);` to `tests/e2e/lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js`, in the Home LIN-4247 test, directly after the `opened-task-running` `toHaveCount(0)` line. Then confirm it passes on the fix and fails with `state.run.item = null;` removed from `endRun` (I observed both).
- **Inside** (the Home/Swipe surfaces named in the plan). No browser test drives a run ending on **Swipe**. The vm units mount `surface: 'swipe'` by default, so the flipped test and the new incomplete, busy and finished tests exercise Swipe's `paintGo` path. The only gap is real-browser rendering. **Before the merge** (optional, cheap): on `/swipe`, press Go on an unfinished card, then take and finish the item with `/api/dispatch/take` and the feedback post. Within 25 s the card's started line should go and Go should return.
- **Inside** (accepted cost, plan "Likeliest ways this breaks"). The poll now runs every 10 s for as long as `sessions.busy` is true. That covers a queued item with no runner, which can last indefinitely. It is the same read and is skipped on hidden tabs. Nothing to settle beyond noting it at merge, as the plan's At merge section asks.
- **Outside.** Making Go's display follow `/state` entirely (`state.go` only for the press), and sharing one "ended" rule with `cadenceStatus`. Close-out should file this from the Survey comment if no ticket exists yet.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger.

The implementation is correct and matches the plan, and its main witnesses are real (mutation-checked). One gap remains: the Home witness doesn't pin the `run.item` clear it was written for, and close-out adds that one-line e2e assertion.

## Close-out — LIN-4247

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2289, squash-merged as `b5cc4c62`, pinned with `--match-head-commit f5a4f157`. Review's verdict was Approve (conditional on the ledger), at `bff94e0b`.

**Changes I made after the approval (nobody reviewed these):**
- `f5a4f157` adds one e2e assertion in `tests/e2e/lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js`, in the Home LIN-4247 test, right after the `opened-task-running` line: `opened-task-queued` has count 0. It answers review's "What CI Did Not Prove" item 1 (Home's `state.run.item` clear). No source change.

**Ledger:**
1. *Inside, Home `run.item` witness*: done. With the assertion in, the Home test passes on the fix. With `state.run.item = null;` removed from `endRun` it fails on exactly that line (`opened-task-queued` still present); source restored after the check. Review observed the same under the `paintRun()` mutation.
2. *Inside, Swipe browser witness (optional, cheap)*: not run. Swipe has no run block; the vm units mount `surface: 'swipe'` and cover its `paintGo` path (flipped test, incomplete, busy, finished-task). What is left: real-browser rendering on `/swipe` only. I did not run it: it needs a signed-in Swipe session with an unfinished card, which I do not have. It is not a post-deploy check that holds the close; any operator can do it by pressing Go on an unfinished `/swipe` card, taking and finishing the item (`/api/dispatch/take`, then the feedback post), and expecting the started line gone and Go back within 25 s.
3. *Inside, accepted cost (poll runs every 10 s while `sessions.busy`, e.g. a queued item with no runner)*: noted here as the plan's At merge asks. It is the same read, skipped on hidden tabs, and ends with the page. No monitor exists or was invented for it.
4. *Outside, Go's display following `/state` entirely and one shared "ended" rule with `cadenceStatus`*: searched `GET /search` for `cadenceStatus`, `state.go`, `endRun` and the `/state` wording; no existing ticket covered it. Filed **LIN-4256** (Low, Improvement + kind:follow-up + front:surfaces; related to LIN-3546 and this ticket). Priority reasoning: nothing broken today, cost is drift paid ticket by ticket.

**Plan's "At merge" notes:** `public/llms.txt:295` and the Go-states comment were updated in the PR. What is left of the three "in progress" answers: `goInProgress` (is a run live or waiting now: press and mount reads), `stageBusy` (`sessions.busy`, hides the step line), the offer's `busy` kind (the server's, from the same gather); the end rule reads `sessions.busy` and `goInProgress` together.

**CI:** green on `f5a4f157` before merge (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, `CI success`; run 42015651342). Not checked after the merge: main's own CI run.

**Deploy and verification on what landed:** harbour.cat footer showed `b5cc4c6`; the served `/prompt-section.js` contains `runEnded`/`endRun` and the served `/llms.txt:295` has the new wording. I then ran `tests/e2e/lin-4048-finished-task-run.spec.js` on the merged main checkout (`b5cc4c62`): 5/5 pass, including the Home and unfinished-task-page LIN-4247 tests and the finished-task no-Go test. I could not drive the production site itself (needs a signed-in session), so that run is local, on the same commit.

**Housekeeping:** description archived first (snapshot `2026-11-05T11:33:05Z`, full 14,328-char description, confirmed via `/snapshots`), then the discharged Implementation Plan body was replaced with a stub; the heading, `fits one session` and `plan-review due:` line are kept word for word. Problem statement, acceptance, anchors and the Survey direction are untouched. LIN-4048, the only related ticket, was already Done. `Bug` label left in place.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was it difficult?** It was moderately hard, and not where the ticket said. The code change was about 40 lines in `runPoll`. The binding point was that "in progress" has three answers (`goInProgress`, `stageBusy`, the offer's `busy`), and the end rule had to agree with the server's. Most of the friction was in the tests. In the vm sandbox, Stop is only reachable on `surface: 'task'`, because Swipe has no run control. An incomplete reply leaves Go at `started`, not `running`. On Home, the filled "Go" is the Next-step rung, which asks for a confirm and dispatches nothing. I needed a throwaway debug spec to find that Run to PR is the press that queues a run.

**2. What I'd have done first.** Open Home in a real browser and log which button posts `/api/dispatch`, before writing the e2e. That cost one failed 30 s run.

**3. What I'd tidy.** `state.go` is built inline in about eight places, each with the same five fields. A `goState(status, notice)` helper would make it read as one state machine. The stale-read guard (`state.go !== reading`) depends on every writer creating a new object. That contract is implicit, and a helper would make it hold by construction. `endRun` also paints twice (`paintState`, then `paintRun` and `paintGo`): harmless, but wasteful.

**4. The ticket if this area were right.** "Go's displayed state follows `/state`; `state.go` holds only the press." The Survey called that "better still". This ticket existed because `state.go` had an entry and no exit.

**5. What the plan got wrong.**
- It said to drop a reply that lands once Go is "no longer started/running". A Stop restarts the poll with the same `running` status, so a status check would have let a stale read through. The guard had to compare object identity.
- Witness 6 ("fails before") could not fail on the old code, which never ended a run. It is only a guard, proven by mutation.
- Witness 3's fixture (`incomplete` with `busy: true`) didn't test the incomplete rule on its own: `busy` alone kept the run alive, and the mutation survived. I added a bare `{ incomplete }` case.
- "Press Go on Home" is the wrong control, as in point 1.

**6. What it left behind.**
- `runEnded` is now a second "ended" rule beside `task-page.js`'s `createPoller` (and `cadenceStatus`). They are closer than before, but still two rules.
- The identity contract on `state.go` lives only in a comment.
- The plan said to file a ticket for "Go follows `/state` entirely" if none existed. I didn't check, and didn't file one: an open loop.
- Nothing new without a home, and `llms.txt` was updated.
- Simpler: `runPoll`'s stop condition is one named rule, not an `else` comment.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** Yes, mostly. The Home part found a cause the task page couldn't show: `state.run.item` keeping the box active when a short run is never seen live. A task-page-only fix would have shipped with Home still broken. Its cost was the Home e2e, about a third of the test effort, including the wrong-button detour. I'd have drawn the line where it was, with the plan's own stale-read and incomplete witnesses specified against mutations rather than "fails before".

relatedIssue.title: Task page offers "Run to PR" on a finished task

issue.title: Go's displayed state should follow /state; state.go kept only for the press (and share one "run ended" rule with cadenceStatus)
